purpose: AR first phase, PR 1 of 3: migrations 0122 (three ar.* permissions, no role grant), 0123 (seven new tables) and 0124 (two approved columns on ar_invoice_lines), plus the AR Business Master impact checker that must arrive with the tables: once ar_invoices exists, Business Master's reserved checker stops answering NOT_INSTALLED and, without a real one, every currency and payment term change fails closed. One MySQL test file pins the approved columns, keys, foreign keys, CHECK constraints and audit triggers, probes each constraint and runs the checker's SQL; one unit file covers the checker's classification and fail-closed paths. Four existing integration files and the catalogue conventions file change only so that the admin claim set and the seed list account for the three new permissions; the Business Master HTTP case now expects the AR checker READY instead of NOT_INSTALLED. No other existing case, assertion or data changes. UAT-001 updates four existing test files that exercise roles, user management, password changes and migration results. Their assertions and claims now match the business permissions held by system-admin, including all three AR permissions. Customer bank and escalation regression checks are retained. G1 extends existing schema and convention tests for 0126: two nullable varchar(50) columns, the active-reference unique index, idempotent application and the catalogued ar.opening.mgmt permission and system-admin grant.
data: arMigrations: 9 cases; each constraint or checker case writes at most 10 rows inside a transaction that is rolled back, with foreign key checks off on that connection only; no customer, shipment or order fixture. arBusinessMasterImpactChecker: 4 unit cases on a fake connection. Existing files: one extra prefix in a permission filter, one extra file name in a list, one expected status. UAT-001 adds 21 grant rows in the existing migrated fixture and updates expected permissions and JWT claims. The case count and application test data are unchanged. G1 adds no test cases. The existing migration fixture includes one additional permission and system-admin grant; existing constraints retain their data.
concurrency: 1 connection per case, serial; no concurrent trial.
thresholds: All cases pass; exact equality on the schema lists; coverage floors unchanged; no timing threshold.
trigger: Existing ci.yml triggers and discovery only: the existing server MySQL integration shards and server test job. No new job, schedule or dispatch. No capacity or performance workload.
cost: Estimated under 1 second for the new files (local run: 0.13 s for 9 MySQL cases, under 0.1 s for 4 unit cases); not measured in CI. No new job.
